text:
oliver: Hey team, Oliver here 44b. New MacBook Air (M2, Ventura). Trying to run the repo bootstrap but hitting a few mac-specific snags: asdf Python and Node builds error out with OpenSSL/linker errors, `brew` install warnings about ARM vs x86 bottles, and VS Code can't access my SSH keys (keychain prompt blocked). Also bootstrap.sh expects `.envrc` and 1Password but my 1Password sign-in isn't finished. Who's best to ping for help?

mei: welcome Oliver! macOS gotchas first: install Xcode Command Line Tools: `xcode-select --install`. Many build failures are just missing CLT.

carl: +1. For openssl, we use Homebrew on Apple Silicon under `/opt/homebrew`. Typical flow I use:

```
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config gpg gnupg pinentry-mac
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib/pkgconfig"
```

Then retry `asdf install python 3.11.4` or `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0`.

oliver: I did install brew but some bottles were x86 and brew warned about running under Rosetta. Do we need Rosetta?

mei: only for certain x86-only tools. Two options: prefer native ARM bottles (`brew install` will choose arm bottles if available), or install Rosetta and run a separate Intel Homebrew if you need x86 packages. To install Rosetta: `softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license`. For most dev work here we try to stick to ARM-native. If a dependency is x86-only, we run that tool under Rosetta.

carl: note for the Node asdf plugin: the plugin uses gpg to verify releases. Make sure `gpg` is available (brew installed) and `gpg --recv-keys` works. If Node builds still fail, set the OpenSSL env vars before the `asdf install` command.

oliver: VS Code prompts for Keychain access but the dialog gets hidden behind the fullscreen window and I accidentally denied it. Now SSH keys won't load. How to fix?

mei: open Keychain Access -> find the item (ssh key / passphrase), right-click -> Get Info -> Access Control -> add `Code` (VS Code) and `Terminal` if you want them to access. Alternatively, re-run the prompt by restarting VS Code and trying an SSH action again; on macOS you'll get a new prompt.

oliver: bootstrap.sh still wants `.envrc` and 1Password. I don't have 1Password CLI access yet. Should I make placeholders?

zoe: yes, copy `env.example` to `.env.local` and create a minimal `.envrc` like:

```
export $(grep -v '^#' .env.local | xargs)
```

then `direnv allow`. That unblocks the script until infra grants secrets. For SSH/GPG we expect you to generate a local keypair: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "oliver@redwood"` and add the pubkey to your account.

oliver: I also saw `npm` native modules failing with `node-gyp` complaining about missing `python` or `make`. I thought asdf node was supposed to bundle that.

carl: on mac you need the CLT (xcode-select) and often `python` from asdf for node-gyp (it uses Python2/3 env). We recommend: install `python` via asdf first, ensure `python3` in PATH, then `npm rebuild` or reinstall packages. Also `brew install pkg-config` helps native builds.

infra-bot: [onboarding] Created ticket ONB-2215 for Oliver to get 1Password + repo permissions. Infra will follow up to add your public key to the onboarding list if needed.

oliver: thanks infra-bot 64f. One last thing: Docker Desktop on M2 seems to refuse some amd64 images in Compose. Any local tips so CI runs similarly?

mei: prefer `--platform linux/amd64` explicitly if you must pull amd64 images, but better is to use multi-arch images or set Docker Desktop to use emulation (qemu) in settings. For CI we typically run things in linux/amd64, so if you need parity run `docker buildx` or use `docker run --platform` locally. If you can, test with the `make ci-local` which uses the same images as CI.

oliver: got it. After installing CLT, brew openssl, gpg, and exporting flags, `asdf install` completed for node and python. I copied `.env.local` (placeholders) and created `.envrc`. VS Code keychain fixed after re-allowing. `make ci-local` ran the fast suite. Thanks everyone 44d. I'll add these mac-specific notes to my onboarding doc.

zoe: welcome aboard! ping me if you want a 20min pairing to walk the codebase and local workflow.
